title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 70-73 of the cote): Grothendieck is reducing a 'relative/integral' form of the section conjecture over a normal base S to statements over traits. U_S is an 'elementary' anabelian relative scheme over S (a successive fibration in hyperbolic curves). The setting is E_X = π_1(X; universal cover) viewed as an extension of E_S = π_1(S). One starts from a section of E_{U_K} over E_K = Gal(K̄/K), with K the function field of S. By the section conjecture over K this gives a rational section (a K-point) of U_S. The question is when this rational section extends to a true section of U_S over S.

The previous page handled codimension ≥ 2. If the section is defined off a closed set Z of codim ≥ 2, then by induction on the elementary fibration one reduces to a relative curve X_S − T. Weil's extension theorem (genus ≥ 1) extends the section to X. The pullback of T is then a divisor that vanishes off Z, hence vanishes. So everything reduces to the codimension-1 points x of S, i.e. to the trait Spec O_x.

This page sets this up.
- Diagram (9) is the tower of schemes S ← Spec O_x ← Spec K ← Spec K̄, with U_S, U_{O_x}, U_K, U_{K̄} and the universal cover Ũ_S above them.
- Diagram (10) is the induced diagram of fundamental groups E_{U_S} ← E_{U_{O_x}} ← E_{U_K} over E_S ← E_{O_x} ← E_K. The squares are claimed cartesian (same geometric kernel π = π_1(U_K̄)) and the horizontal maps surjective.
- A homomorphism E_K → E_{U_S} lifting E_K → E_S is the same as a lift φ_x: E_K → E_{U_{O_x}} of E_K → E_{O_x}, composed with the canonical map E_{U_{O_x}} → E_{U_S}. By cartesianness, such lifts correspond bijectively to sections of E_{U_K} over E_K, i.e. to lifts of E_K → E_S into E_{U_S}.
- The key claim to prove: φ_x kills the inertia group I_x. Equivalently, φ_x factors through E_{O_x}. The margin notes that E_K modulo the closed normal subgroup generated by I_x is π_1(Spec O_x), since O_x is normal of dimension 1.
- So φ_x comes from a section of E_{U_{O_x}} over E_{O_x}. This should hold iff the corresponding rational section of U_S/S is defined at x.

The next page abstracts this into a 'Theorem (?)' over a trait T, for an elementary anabelian U/T. In substance: a Galois section of the generic fibre that is unramified (factors through π_1(T)) corresponds to a K-point extending to a T-point (integral point, 'good reduction' of the section).
errors: The text writes 'E_K ← E_{U_S}' but the intended homomorphism is E_K → E_{U_S} (a lift of E_K → E_S); the direction is a slip.

The claim that the squares in (10) are cartesian requires the kernel of E_{U_{O_x}} → E_{O_x} to equal π_1(U_K̄). If the residue field at x has characteristic p > 0, this kernel is only a (tame/specialization) quotient of π_1(U_K̄), and the squares need not be cartesian. The argument is safe when S lives over Q (all residue characteristics 0), presumably the intended setting.

The equivalence 'φ_x kills I_x ⇔ the rational section is defined at x' is only announced, not proved. One direction (a point extends ⇒ the section is unramified) is easy. The converse is the substantive 'theorem' formulated on the next page and is not established here.

ideas.what: Reduction of extending a Galois section/rational point over a normal base S to codimension-1 points (traits), via purity of the branch locus (E_K/⟨I_x⟩ = π_1(O_x)) together with Weil's extension theorem and the codim ≥ 2 argument from the previous page
ideas.modern_name: Integral/relative section conjecture over higher-dimensional normal bases; purity (Zariski–Nagata) reduction to DVRs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Purity: Zariski–Nagata, SGA1/SGA2. Integral versions of the section conjecture are discussed e.g. by J. Stix (unsure of precise attribution).
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture and relative/finiteness consequences, but this specific reduction is not there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Criterion: a section of π_1(U_K) → G_K gives an integral point at x iff the induced lift kills inertia I_x, i.e. factors through π_1(U_{O_x}) over π_1(O_x)
ideas.modern_name: Unramified sections ↔ integral points / Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich-type criterion for sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian geometry; treated in Stix's work on the section conjecture (unsure of exact source)

ideas.what: Cartesian description of fundamental group extensions along S ← O_x ← K: lifts E_K → E_{U_{O_x}} ↔ sections of E_{U_K} ↔ lifts E_K → E_{U_S}
ideas.modern_name: Base change of homotopy exact sequences

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a proof strategy for the 'integral' section conjecture over arbitrary normal bases S. The strategy reduces, via purity and Weil's extension theorem, to a statement over traits for elementary anabelian schemes of any relative dimension. The trait statement (unramified section ⇒ point extends) is left as 'Théorème (?)'. Over traits with residue characteristic p it is subtle and in general not established (it is tied to the section conjecture itself).
missed.quote: j'ai envie de prouver que φ_x : E_K → E_{U_{O_x}} s'annule sur I_x, i.e. provient d'une section de E_{U_{O_x}} sur O_x
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck formulating the relative/integral section conjecture for higher-dimensional elementary anabelian schemes over higher-dimensional bases, and an explicit reduction to DVRs. It is a modest documentary point on how he envisaged the section conjecture beyond curves over number fields; mathematically largely anticipated by later work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a standard reduction (cartesian diagrams of π_1-extensions, purity to pass to traits) in service of an integral form of the section conjecture. It is historically interesting as an early formulation for elementary anabelian schemes over normal bases, but the ideas are known or folklore today.
transcription_corrections: 'L'hom[?] E_K ← E_{U_S}' should read 'L'homomorphisme E_K → E_{U_S}' (the arrow direction in the text is a slip).
'SS3[?] La section rationnelle correspond.t à de U_S 13[?] est définie en x' plausibly reads 'ssi la section rationnelle correspondante de U_S/S est définie en x' ('13' ≈ '/S').
Margin: plausibly 'NB Le quotient de E_K par le sg. [normal] engendré par I_x est ... (O_x normal ...) i.e. E_{O_x} = π_1(Spec O_x)'.
On the next page 'ambitieux[?]' is almost certainly 'anabélien'.
